match.reason: The new point combines relative scarcity, opportunity cost and the PPF with the three economic questions (what, how and for whom to produce), and neither bank point covers the three questions, so a separate point is needed.

draft.title: Relative scarcity and the PPF
card: Needs and wants are unlimited, but resources are limited. This is relative scarcity, and it forces every economy to make choices.
Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up when a choice is made. Choosing one use of resources means going without another.

A production possibility frontier (PPF) shows the most of two goods an economy can produce with its resources and technology. A point on the curve uses all resources fully. A point inside the curve leaves some unused. A point outside is not possible.

Moving along the PPF shows opportunity cost: more of one good means less of the other. Where the economy sits on the PPF answers the three economic questions: what to produce, how to produce it and who gets it.
draft.remember: Resources are limited, so every choice has an opportunity cost. The PPF shows the trade-off.

a.q: An economy moves along its PPF to make more wheat. What does the move show?
opts: Less of the other good can be made
More resources have become available
Some resources are now left unused
Technology has improved for both goods
a.why: Along the PPF, resources are fully used, so more wheat means giving up some of the other good. That lost output is the opportunity cost. More resources or better technology would move the whole frontier outwards, not move along it.
a.clue: On the curve, all resources are already in use.

b.q: Tariq's country makes only tractors and cars. It is at a point inside its PPF. What does this show?
opts: Some resources are unused or not fully employed
The country is making the best mix of the two goods
The country has run out of resources to use
The country can reach this point only with new technology
b.why: A point inside the PPF means the economy could make more of one or both goods with the resources it has. Some are idle or poorly used. A point outside, not inside, would need new technology or more resources.
b.clue: Compare the point with the curve, which shows the most that can be made.

a.best: Less of the other good can be made

b.best: Some resources are unused or not fully employed

problems.detail: The card says where the economy sits on the PPF answers all three economic questions, including 'who gets it'. A PPF shows what to produce and, by being on or inside the curve, whether resources are fully used. It does not show how output is shared among people. Reword to say the PPF illustrates the choices about what to produce and how much of each, rather than claiming a point on it answers 'who gets it'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear right answer each. The card overstates the PPF by saying a point on it answers 'who gets it', when a PPF does not show how output is shared.
